verdict.rationale: Runpod's Pod docs say users can connect via JupyterLab or VS Code/Cursor for local IDE integration, and official templates come with JupyterLab preconfigured. However, the evidence never documents a one-step connection flow, and community remarks that the environment is locked down concern third-party remote-kernel setups, not these documented access paths. missing for 10: evidence of a one-click/one-step Jupyter or IDE connection flow, detailed VS Code/Cursor setup documentation, independent hands-on corroboration

support.subject: As a developer, I can open Jupyter or connect my IDE (VS Code/Cursor) to the instance in one step

citations.quote: you can connect to your Pod through SSH for command-line access, web proxy for exposed web services, JupyterLab for data science workflows, or VS Code/Cursor for local IDE integration
Access your Pod via SSH, JupyterLab, or VS Code.
Instead of installing PyTorch, configuring JupyterLab, and setting up all dependencies yourself, you can select an official Runpod PyTorch template and have everything ready to go instantly.
